summary: A dense Uwe Rosenberg building-and-engine game where players buy hexes, erect production buildings, and chain resource conversions to churn out high-value goods like whiskey, bricks, and relics. It plays like a heavier, more interlocking cousin of Agricola/Le Havre with less randomness and more spatial puzzle-solving about where buildings go.
praised: Strong replayability via the alternate Ireland/religious building sets
criticised: Long downtime in multiplayer, especially with 4
Steep learning curve and rulebook complexity
Can feel solitaire-ish with little direct interaction

interaction.detail: Players compete for a shared row of action/building spaces so taking one denies it to others that round, but the bulk of the game happens on each player's private board of hexes and buildings. There's no direct attack on opponents' resources or scores.

scoring.why: Final score sums printed building victory points, prestige goods (books, ceramics, ornaments, relics), converted leftover coins, and penalties for unused land, so no single system dominates.
scoring.how_you_win: Build an efficient chain of production buildings that turns raw resources into high-value prestige goods and point-earning structures, then finish with the highest combined total of building VPs, goods, and money.
